title: Bulk smithsonite DFT optimization
action: Starting from the experimental lattice parameters (a=b=4.6528 Å, c=15.025 Å, α=β=90°, γ=120°), perform density functional theory (DFT) optimization of the bulk smithsonite crystal structure using a GGA functional with dispersion correction.
description: Obtain optimized lattice constants needed for surface slab construction.

title: Perfect (101) surface slab construction and relaxation
action: Cleave the optimized bulk crystal to expose the (101) surface, create a (2×2×1) slab with five atomic layers and a vacuum layer, then relax the slab allowing the top two layers to move while fixing the bottom three.
description: Generate the reference perfect surface structure.

title: Defective and impurity surface construction and relaxation
action: Construct Zn‑vacancy (VT) and Fe‑impurity (TFe) smithsonite (101) surface slabs from the relaxed perfect slab, then relax each using the same DFT settings.
description: Create the defect/impurity surface models for H₂O adsorption.

title: Bare surface electronic analysis (PDOS, electron density)
action: Compute partial density of states (PDOS) and electron density for the relaxed perfect, VT, and TFe surfaces.
description: Characterize the electronic structure of the clean surfaces; evidence may be logged as optional artifact.

title: Isolated H₂O molecule optimization
action: Optimize an isolated H₂O molecule in a periodic box at the same DFT level.
description: Obtain the reference H₂O energy and geometry for adsorption calculations.

title: DFT H₂O adsorption calculations
action: Perform geometry relaxation of H₂O adsorption complexes on perfect (TZn, BZn sites), VT‑vacancy, and TFe‑impurity surfaces using the relaxed slabs and optimized H₂O.
description: Obtain total energies and relaxed adsorption geometries.

title: Analysis of DFT adsorption energies and forms (scored)
action: Compute the adsorption energy for each site as E_ad = E(slab+H₂O) – E(slab) – E(H₂O). Determine the adsorption form (dissociative if O–H bond is broken, molecular otherwise) from the final geometry. Write the results to a CSV file.
description: CSV file with columns: surface_name, site, adsorption_energy_eV, adsorption_form. One row per calculated surface.
output_schema: surface_name (string, e.g. 'perfect', 'VT_defect', 'TFe_impurity'), site (string, e.g. 'TZn', 'BZn', 'VT', 'TFe'), adsorption_energy_eV (float, unit: eV), adsorption_form (string, one of 'dissociative' or 'molecular')

title: Post‑adsorption electronic analysis (PDOS, electron density difference, Mulliken populations)
action: Compute PDOS of bonding atoms, electron density difference maps, and Mulliken bond populations for the optimized adsorption complexes.
description: Electronic‑structure evidence supporting the adsorption forms; results may be logged as optional evidence.

title: DFT pre‑optimization of spherical water cluster
action: Pre‑optimize a 13‑molecule spherical water cluster using DFT in a periodic box to obtain atomic charges for subsequent MD force‑field calculations.
description: Generate initial charges for MD with the universal force field.

title: MD simulation of water cluster on surfaces
action: Run NVT molecular dynamics at 298 K for 500 ps using the universal force field (UFF) to simulate a water cluster on perfect, VT‑vacancy, and TFe‑impurity surfaces.
description: Generate MD trajectories from which wetting energies are extracted.

title: Analysis of MD adsorption and cohesive energies (scored)
action: From MD trajectories, compute the average adsorption energy and average cohesive energy per water molecule for each surface. Write the results to a CSV file.
description: CSV file with columns: surface_name, md_adsorption_energy_kcal_per_mol, md_cohesive_energy_kcal_per_mol. One row per calculated surface.
output_schema: surface_name (string), md_adsorption_energy_kcal_per_mol (float, unit: kcal/mol), md_cohesive_energy_kcal_per_mol (float, unit: kcal/mol)
